svg.title: Cash Conversion Cycle Gates
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-cash-cycle-gates; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: Cash Conversion Cycle Gates; subtitle: Inventory days plus sales days minus payable days, checked before cash leaves; caption: Kurtis Hanni cut a client's cycle from 230 to 45 days, slashing required cash from $235,000 to $67,000; LedgerGurus typically sees e-commerce cycles of at least 90 days.; assumptions note: Gate order runs from purchasing through exit. The 37.2% figure is One Minute Finance's annualized cost of letting a 2/10 net 30 discount lapse.; note: Sources: Kurtis Hanni [0WBeNhRVKHY @ 00:09:32; 00:11:29], One Minute Finance [7yuWFm95LDw @ 00:07:28], LedgerGurus [F-Y1cubdesE @ 00:06:24], Brent Freeman - The CBB Group [KSfESWIcDGI @ 00:09:41].; nodes: gate: G1; question: Does cash cover the full cycle before an overseas order with zero payable days?; pass next: G2; fail action: Hold the order and negotiate billing on arrival; the 230-day client needed $235,000 out before a dollar returned.; gate: G2; question: Is every 2/10 net 30 early-pay discount being captured?; pass next: G3; fail action: Pay within 10 days; holding cash 20 extra days costs 37.2% annualized.; gate: G3; question: Has net 60 wholesale been modeled for the receivables jump and inventory build?; pass next: G4; fail action: Model receivables and inventory before signing; revenue can sit on the books without the cash.; gate: G4; question: Before going to market, is the 12- to 24-month average working capital computed?; pass next: Proceed to sale; fail action: Compute the average and pull excess capital out, or the buyer negotiates to keep it.

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Does cash cover the full cycle before an overseas order with zero payable days?; pass next: G2; fail action: Hold the order and negotiate billing on arrival; the 230-day client needed $235,000 out before a dollar returned.
gate: G2; question: Is every 2/10 net 30 early-pay discount being captured?; pass next: G3; fail action: Pay within 10 days; holding cash 20 extra days costs 37.2% annualized.

gate: G3; question: Has net 60 wholesale been modeled for the receivables jump and inventory build?; pass next: G4; fail action: Model receivables and inventory before signing; revenue can sit on the books without the cash.

gate: G4; question: Before going to market, is the 12- to 24-month average working capital computed?; pass next: Proceed to sale; fail action: Compute the average and pull excess capital out, or the buyer negotiates to keep it.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order runs from purchasing through exit. The 37.2% figure is One Minute Finance's annualized cost of letting a 2/10 net 30 discount lapse.
